summary:
Astrolytics is an AI-powered dashboard developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to explore fire behavior and identify gaps in NASA’s combustion research.

Using 593 NASA PSI combustion tests, it visualizes how oxygen concentration and pressure affect flames across Earth, the ISS, and lunar habitats. It also ranks 20 investigations, summarizes findings using AI, and highlights missing experimental data.

Our goal is to make NASA research accessible and support safer space habitats and future human exploration.
details:
Astrolytics is an interactive, AI-powered dashboard that makes NASA’s combustion research easier to explore, understand, and apply to real-world fire safety challenges.

Our project brings together data from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database, organizing 593 combustion tests into an interactive Fire Map that shows how oxygen concentration and pressure relate to flame behavior. Users can explore different environments, including Earth, the International Space Station, and Moon bases, or create their own custom habitat by adjusting environmental conditions.

We also developed a transparent scoring system that ranks 20 combustion investigations based on how closely their conditions match the selected environment and how useful they are for fire safety research. AI helps summarize and interpret complex scientific information, while our team checks the results against NASA’s original sources to maintain scientific accuracy.

One of our project's most important features is identifying research gaps. Instead of simply showing existing data, Astrolytics highlights conditions that have not been tested or where experimental evidence is limited. This helps users understand what scientists already know and what still needs further investigation.

We developed a web-based dashboard hosted on GitHub Pages, using NASA’s scientific datasets, data cleaning and visualization techniques, and AI-assisted analysis. We standardized different pressure units, organized experimental results, and made the information accessible through interactive visualizations.

What makes Astrolytics different is its focus on both existing knowledge and missing evidence. Our goal is to make NASA’s research accessible to a wide audience, from students and the general public to scientists, engineers, and future Moon base designers, while supporting safer space habitats, better fire protection systems, and future scientific discoveries.
